title: Elastic reservations: simplify SKU tiers, contract language, and security QnA matrix
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal: Define a simplified, sales-friendly set of Dedicated capacity SKUs that support elastic reservations (baseline commit + burst credits + short autoscale buffer) and a companion security QnA matrix for enterprise contracting. This ticket covers finalizing SKU definitions, pricing curves for burst usage, contract term language templates, and the canonical Security/Compliance QnA to attach to EA/SAQs.

Background: Sales and legal report that current commit options are too granular and that enterprise buyers are asking for clearer burst economics plus a succinct security package for procurement. Engineering has a working autoscale prototype and the runtime team has perf profiles for common models at different quantization levels. We need an actionable, low-friction SKU catalog with legal-friendly wording and a single-page security matrix for fast procurement.

Scope:
- SKU catalog: 3 reserve bands (Foundation, Performance, Enterprise) + burst credits bucketed by % of baseline and minute-based burst throttles.
- Pricing curves: per-GPU reserved monthly price, burst credit unit price, and per-token overage fallback pricing for hosted variants.
- SLA tiers: Bronze/Silver/Gold with quantifiable latency P95 and availability windows and clearly articulated fallbacks (model downgrade, regional failover).
- Autoscale buffer policy: recommended default buffer minutes, bursting prioritization, and cost caps.
- Contract template copy snippets: Master Service Agreement language for surge credits, preemption, and data isolation.
- Security QnA: single-sheet answers for common buyer questions (data residency, KMS, SOC2, pen test, SAML/SCIM, audit logs).

Why now: Q2 enterprise pipeline has 6 inbound deals requesting clearer burst terms and a short security package. Standardizing will reduce legal cycles and improve win rates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SKU catalog spreadsheet with SKU IDs, baseline capacity (GPUs), memory, expected throughput, and recommended models; 2) Pricing doc with committed monthly price, burst unit price, and example invoices for 3 customer profiles; 3) Contract snippets validated by Legal that cover surge credits, preemption, and termination; 4) Security QnA matrix (<=2 pages) reviewed by Security with answers and references to SOC2, KMS/HSM, VPC options; 5) Sales enablement one-pager and FAQ; 6) Internal runtime checklist for mapping model perf profiles to SKU bands.
success_metrics: - Reduce average negotiation cycles for Dedicated deals from 18 to <=12 business days; - Increase win rate on enterprise POCs asking for burst terms by 15% within one quarter; - <= 10 legal follow-up questions on security QnA in pilot contracts; - Documented cost per 1M tokens for each SKU band and observed deviation <10% in pilot customers.
rollout_plan: 1) Draft SKU+pricing and security QnA -> 2) Legal & Security reviews (2 weeks) -> 3) Internal sales pilot with 3 current prospective customers (2 weeks) -> 4) Revise pricing/terms based on observed surge patterns and legal feedback -> 5) Publish SKU catalog and sales one-pager, update Console product dropdown and billing mapping. Target general availability by release tag dedicated-2026.04.
implementation_notes:
Trade-offs considered: a) Narrow SKU set reduces complexity for sales but limits price granularity for high-variance workloads; b) Burst as credits simplifies billing but requires a clear throttling policy to avoid noisy neighbor impact; c) Autoscale buffer defaults will be conservative to protect latency SLOs; engineering will implement a per-tenant cost cap and soft-notify when burst consumption reaches 50/80/100% of buffer.

Engineering hooks needed: mapping SKU IDs to node pool types, autoscale policy defaults, telemetry counters for burst credit consumption, and billing event tags to reconcile consumed burst credits vs reserved baseline. Runtime team provided perf profiles here: https://redwood.internal/docs/runtime/perf-profiles-2026-Q1 (internal).
open_questions: - What explicit burst throttle (% of baseline) is acceptable for Gold SLA vs Silver?; - Should burst credits be time-limited (e.g., must be consumed within 12 months) or evergreen?; - Legal: acceptable wording for 'non-guaranteed burst' vs 'guaranteed baseline' in the MSA?; - Security: are there additional QnA items required for EU public sector customers?; - Sales: pricing sensitivity for startups vs enterprise (list discounts or seat-based add-ons)?
timeline: 2026-02-10: kickoff and discovery; 2026-02-17: draft SKU catalog and initial pricing curves; 2026-02-24: Legal intake; 2026-03-03: Security review of QnA; 2026-03-10: Sales pilot launch with two opportunities; 2026-03-24: Collect pilot feedback and finalize docs; 2026-04-05: finalize contract snippets and publish rollout.
